title.en: Torque, angular momentum and equilibrium of a rigid body
title.kn: ಬಲಭ್ರಾಮಕ, ಕೋನೀಯ ಸಂವೇಗ ಮತ್ತು ದೃಢ ಕಾಯದ ಸಮತೋಲನ

heading.en: Why is the door handle far from the hinges?

hook.en: Push a door near its hinges and it hardly moves. Push at the handle with the same force and it swings open. The turning effect depends on where you push.
hook.kn: ಕೀಲುಗಳ ಹತ್ತಿರ ಬಾಗಿಲನ್ನು ತಳ್ಳಿದರೆ ಅದು ಕದಲುವುದೇ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಅದೇ ಬಲವನ್ನು ಹಿಡಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಾಕಿದರೆ ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ ತೆರೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ತಿರುಗಿಸುವ ಪರಿಣಾಮ ಎಲ್ಲಿ ತಳ್ಳುತ್ತೇವೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ.

narration.en: Push a door near its hinges and it hardly moves. Push at the handle with the same force and it swings open. The turning effect depends on where you push.

body.en: Torque, or the moment of a force, is $\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec F$, with magnitude $rF\sin\theta$: the force times its perpendicular distance from the axis. The angular momentum of a particle is $\vec l = \vec r\times\vec p$. Just as $\vec F = d\vec p/dt$, we have $\vec\tau = d\vec L/dt$, so with zero external torque the angular momentum is conserved.
body.kn: ಬಲಭ್ರಾಮಕ τ = r × F, ಪರಿಮಾಣ rF sinθ: ಬಲ × ಅಕ್ಷದಿಂದ ಅದರ ಲಂಬ ದೂರ. ಕಣದ ಕೋನೀಯ ಸಂವೇಗ l = r × p. τ = dL/dt; ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲಭ್ರಾಮಕ ಶೂನ್ಯವಾದರೆ ಕೋನೀಯ ಸಂವೇಗ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಿತ.

points.en: Unit of torque: N m (dimensions [ML²T⁻²], like work)
Unit of angular momentum: kg m² s⁻¹ (= J s)

title.en: Equilibrium of a rigid body and the principle of moments

body.en: A rigid body is in mechanical equilibrium when both the net external force and the net external torque are zero. For a lever this gives the principle of moments: load × load arm = effort × effort arm. A couple, two equal and opposite forces not on the same line, produces a torque but no net force. The centre of gravity is the point about which the total torque of gravity is zero.
body.kn: ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲ ಮತ್ತು ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಬಲಭ್ರಾಮಕ ಎರಡೂ ಶೂನ್ಯವಾದಾಗ ದೃಢ ಕಾಯ ಯಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಸನ್ನೆಗೆ ಭ್ರಾಮಕಗಳ ತತ್ವ: ಭಾರ × ಭಾರದ ತೋಳು = ಯತ್ನ × ಯತ್ನದ ತೋಳು. ಯುಗ್ಮವು ಬಲಭ್ರಾಮಕ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ ಆದರೆ ನಿವ್ವಳ ಬಲ ನೀಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

points.en: Mechanical advantage = effort arm / load arm
A couple gives rotation without translation
Centre of gravity = CM when g is uniform

problem.en: A uniform metre stick is balanced on a knife-edge at its 50 cm mark. A 20 g mass hangs at the 10 cm mark. Where must a 40 g mass be hung to balance it?

steps.en: The stick's own weight acts at the pivot, so it gives no torque.
Moments about the pivot: 20 × (50 − 10) = 40 × d, so d = 20 cm.
The 40 g mass goes 20 cm on the other side: at the 70 cm mark.

heading.en: Line through the axis? No turn

body.en: Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action. If the line of action of a force passes through the axis, its torque is zero however large the force is.
